newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lyonnaise sees 1996 profit rebound - head.
newsitem.headline: Lyonnaise sees 1996 profit rebound - head.

text.p: French utilities giant Lyonnaise des Eaux expects a rebound in profit this year, chairman Jerome Monod said on Friday.
"There will be a rebound in the first-half results and perhaps the full-year, which will be significant," he told an investment conference, but declined to give further details.

Turnover for the 1996 first-half was 44.47 billion francs ($8.8 billion) versus 43.95 billion a year ago. The group posted 1995 net attributable profit of 906 million francs, compared to 1.06 billion, on turnover of 98.62 billion francs.

The company aims for a return on capital of more than 10 percent, with a target of 12 percent in 1998. In the 1996 first half, the return was nine percent, compared to 8.1 for full-year 1995, Monod said.
He did not rule out a drop in turnover in the next few years, which would be a good thing, as non-profitable subsidiaries are sold.
The company faces difficulties in the construction business and wants to dispose of assets, especially abroad. "There will certainly be sales of subsidiaries," he said.

The company wants to concentrate on environmental services, construction and concessions, and communications. It will develop in the latter through cable operations and through its stake in the M6 channel and the Television Par Satellite (TPS) digital TV consortium.
The improvement in profitability will come through a reduction in cyclical risk, particularly in the building and public works sector, which accounts for 20 percent of group turnover, Monod said.
